title: Crusaders Sack Béziers and the Cathar War Begins
dek: On 22 July 1209 the army Innocent III raised against the Cathars storms Béziers and kills Catholics and heretics alike. Twenty years later Languedoc is bound to the French crown.
body: A later story has the legate, asked how to tell Catholics from heretics, answer: kill them all, the Lord knows his own. Historians doubt he said it.

panels.label: Arnaud Amalric Said
panels.text: The legate Arnaud Amalric told Innocent III that the crusaders spared no one in Béziers, put almost 20,000 to the sword, and that divine vengeance raged against the city.

panels.label: Trencavel Said
panels.text: Raymond Roger Trencavel, viscount of Béziers, said he was a loyal member of the Church and, being young, not to blame for the heresy in his lands.

panels.label: The Stakes
panels.text: Each side said it stood with the Church; at stake was who would rule Languedoc and police its faith, the pope’s legates and northern barons or the southern lords.
